subject: Nanotechnology
title: Molecular Machines
description: A short lesson to help you apply Molecular Machines.

hook.text: A molecule that spins like a motor, walks like feet, or opens like a switch — molecular machines won the 2016 Nobel Prize.

buildup.text: Sauvage, Stoddart, and Feringa built rotaxanes, catenanes, and molecular rotors — interlocked rings that move on command.

discovery.text: A rotaxane is a ring threaded on an axle — chemical signals slide the ring between stations, a molecular shuttle.

twist.text: Making one machine is easy — coordinating billions simultaneously to do useful macroscopic work remains unsolved.

climax.text: Researchers embedded molecular motors in liquid crystal films — light-driven rotation changed surface texture visibly.

punchline.text: Chemistry built the smallest machines — now it must teach them to work together.

quiz.question: What is a rotaxane?
options: A nanoparticle that rotates in an electric field
A molecular architecture where a ring is threaded on an axle and can be shuttled between positions
A rotating enzyme found in cell membranes
